about: How each pull request was checked, as recorded in its description on GitHub. These numbers are not computed at build time; each entry links to its source.

prs.title: Model, tokenizer, tests and CI
prs.check: 28 deliberately broken versions of the model and tokenizer (wrong attention scaling, missing LayerNorm, no position embeddings, temperature mistakes and more): every one makes a test fail.

prs.title: Data pipeline for the three books
prs.check: 12 kinds of deliberate damage to the data (swapped verses, a Yusuf Ali verse in place of Pickthall's, a stray digit, a truncated verse and more): the tests catch all 12. The pipeline gives byte-identical output on every run.

prs.title: Training, sampling, and the eval harness
prs.check: 58 hand-written mutants of the training loop, sampling, eval reports and suffix array: each one makes at least one test fail. A 300-step smoke run of the full model, and a killed run that resumed at the right step.

prs.title: Training results, eval report and samples
prs.check: A test keeps the README's result tables in sync with the eval JSON, so a number cannot drift from its source.

ci: GitHub Actions runs the Python tests on every pull request and every push to main, with CPU-only PyTorch. This website adds a second job: install, typecheck, unit tests, build and browser smoke tests.

web.about: 95 Vitest unit tests and 4 Playwright smoke tests for the website: the forward pass against PyTorch logits, greedy generation token for token, the tokenizer against Python, the advice state machine and the data loaders.
